blindSummary: Same-sex conduct is legal in this country — unusual for its world region — but reporting by a foreign broadcaster documents that LGBT people must hide to keep their jobs and live in peace; there is no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination law, and no visible community outside the capital. No documented pattern of police targeting trans people.
blindOutOfScope: Thin data; legal but closeted profile.
blindSourceSummaries: A foreign broadcaster's report (Aug 2024): same-sex relations are legal here but widely considered socially unacceptable, forcing LGBT people to hide to keep jobs and live in peace — with their own networks, body language and dialect.

A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: documents the post-coup regime, unlawful killings, and 'societal discrimination and violence against women, persons with disabilities, and the lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBT) community'.

A foreign broadcaster's audience-language service (July 2020): an explainer on decriminalisation and LGBT rights across this country's world region - which states in the region have decriminalised (one joining around 22 of 53 in the region), with penalties of 10+ years elsewhere; regional context for this country.
An LGBT travel-guide site: country guide covering the legal situation (legal but unequal age of consent) and travel considerations.

A rights campaign publication tracking criminalisation worldwide (July 2025): this country rejected UN UPR recommendations to combat anti-LGBT violence and hate speech and to equalise the age of consent; six domestic organisations protested: 'Refusing to act is to endorse impunity and condone violence.'

An asylum-law resource platform's country entry on LGBTQI+ support: legal framework - homosexual activity legal but a penal-code provision sets a different age of consent for same-sex acts; public attitudes, state protection capacity, case law, supporting organisations and country-of-origin experts.
